newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat against extraditing Hamas leader to Israel.
newsitem.headline: Arafat against extraditing Hamas leader to Israel.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has asked the United States to refrain from extraditing a top leader of the Islamic militant Hamas group to Israel, an aide said on Thursday.
The request came as pressure piled up on Washington not to hand over Mousa Abu Marzook, the political leader of Hamas, to Israel after he withdrew a court appeal against his extradition.
"President Arafat yesterday asked the U.S. administration not to hand over Dr Mousa Abu Marzook to Israel," the aide, Nabil Abu Rdainah told Reuters.
He declined to give any details on the request.

Abu Marzook, a native of the Gaza Strip, has been held in New York since immigration officials detained him in July 1995 after he arrived in the United States, where he had lived for at least 15 years.
Israel said it wanted Washington to extradite him to stand trial for alleged responsibility for attacks by Hamas that killed scores of Israelis.

Abu Marzook's lawyers said in New York on Wednesday the Hamas leader had decided to withdraw an appeal against his extradition. His decision means that he can be handed over to Israel within about 60 days.
Hamas officials in Gaza and members of Arafat's Palestinian Authority have warned Washington against extraditing Abu Marzook.
Arafat aide Marwan Kanafani said the United States "would be committing a grave mistake" if it handed over Abu Marzook.

"The American government must give Abu Marzook the right to return to his country or to go to any other place he chooses, especially since he had not been accused of any violations under American law," Kanafani told Reuters.
Palestinian Communications Minister Imad Falouji, a former Hamas leader, warned against the consequences of an extradition.

"If Israel is concerned for its security then it should not accept to take Abu Marzook," he told Reuters. "If Abu Marzook is handed over (to Israel) the impact would be negative on the whole region...I demand he be immediately freed to spare the area a wave of violence we can do without."

Hamas, in a leaflet faxed to an international news agency, compared a handover of Abu Marzook to the 1996 assassination of bombmaker Yahya Ayyash, whose death brought about four suicide bombings in Israel.

"We in Hamas assert to our enduring people and our nation that the handover of Abu Marzook, just like the assassination of martyr hero Yahya Ayyash will not stop the march of resistance and holy war," the statement said.
On Wednesday, Hamas officials in self-ruled Gaza warned the extradition could threaten the fragile calm in "the whole Islamic area."

"We warn the USA that it will bear the whole responsibility of the status of unrest which will emerge as a result of handing Dr Marzook to Israel," Hamas spokesman in Gaza Mahmoud al-Zahhar told a news conference on Wednesday.
The extradition "would place America as an enemy of Islamic people everywhere, because kidnapping Mousa Abu Marzook and sending him to Israel is an act against all Moslems," he said.
